chapter: Depression gigs, Lil Armstrong, joining Chick Webb
title: Club job in Albany, New York
summary: Booking agent Charlie Green sent McRae to a gangster-run club in Albany to join a clarinetist from Philadelphia.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: And then when Chick finally got into the SAVOY you know --
Well in '35 -- I think I told you '35 or '36 -- the winter of '36 -- '35 -- I went to Albany, New York.
They sent for me -- Charlie Green, the booking agent, called me and said, "Look, I want you to go up to Albany, New York. It's a club up there, they need a tenor player up there."
In my next interview, I'm going to tell you the musicians who I worked -- who I met in Albany, New York.
You asked me about some outstanding musicians. There's one clarinet player, a little red-faced guy, real light. But he was an excellent musician.
And I can't think of his name, but he was one of the outstanding musicians around Philly at that time.
If I could call his name, you'd probably
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
know. He's in one of these books. He was in Albany.
I went to Albany and I say "What you doing up in Albany?" (inaudible) -- you know, he moved from Philly up to Albany. He was playing up there.
And I went up there, and he had the band in this club. And I worked with him in Albany in this club.

And this club was controlled by a bunch of gangsters too. And Charlie Green, the booking agent in New York, say, "Look, you can only stay there for a little while, because I want you to go there, because I'm eventually going to send you to Buffalo."
